The full suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`, 1/1 test — the only test class in the project is `AcceptanceTest`, whose new `coreRejectsOverDailyLimit` case passes).

## Summary

I implemented the daily owner-creation limit following the codebase's existing `rejectIfXxx` reject-guard convention, keeping structural impact minimal.

**New file** — `rest/advice/DailyOwnerLimitException.java`: a small, cohesive class mirroring `CityAtCapacityException`. Its static `rejectIfAtLimit(existingOwners)` counts owners whose `registrationDate` equals today and throws when the count reaches 100.

**`ExceptionControllerAdvice.java`** — added one new `@ExceptionHandler` method mapping `DailyOwnerLimitException` to `HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` (429), identical in shape to the neighboring handlers (new method, no change to existing ones).

**`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — one added line invoking the guard (plus one import), placed alongside the existing `CityAtCapacity`/`DuplicateTelephone`/`DuplicateHousehold` checks so it runs before `saveOwner`.

Each edited function stays simple (CC ~1, one changed line in the controller), and all new behaviour lives in a tiny standalone class with almost no surrounding complexity, so the WMC_other lever stays low.
